meta.title: SolidJS Performance & TypeScript Development Guide
meta.purpose: LLM assistant reference for high-performance SolidJS development

principle.title: Fine-Grained Reactivity
principle.description: SolidJS updates only the exact DOM nodes that need to change
principle.rule: Always access signals/stores inside tracking scopes (JSX, createEffect, createMemo)

principle.title: Immutable Updates
principle.description: Never mutate signals or stores directly
principle.rule: Use setters and store utilities (produce, batch) for all updates

principle.title: Update Batching
principle.description: Group multiple updates to prevent excessive re-renders
principle.rule: Use batch() for multiple synchronous updates

bad.code: const screenPos = transform.worldToScreen(props.position); return <div style={{ left: `${screenPos.x}px` }} />;

problems.problem: Calculated once, never updates when props.position changes
Console logs in hot paths kill performance

utility.name: batch
utility.purpose: Group multiple updates into single re-render

when-to-use.use-case: Drag operations with position + visual state

usage.code: const snapshot = unwrap(store); console.log(snapshot); // Safe to use outside tracking scope

utility.name: reconcile
utility.purpose: Efficiently merge new data with existing store

philosophy.title: TypeScript: Tool, Not Master
philosophy.rule: TypeScript should accelerate development, not hinder it
Use 'any' strategically when types are more trouble than they're worth
Focus on business logic first, types second

fix.problem: Property doesn't exist on type errors

development-workflow.step: Build feature with minimal types (use 'any' liberally)
Only fix type errors that provide real value

strategy.name: progressive-typing
utility-first-types
escape-hatches

anti-pattern.name: excessive-console-logging
anti-pattern.description: Console logs in render loops kill performance

anti-pattern.name: breaking-reactivity
anti-pattern.description: Accessing reactive values outside tracking scopes

bad.code: const position = store.position; // Breaks reactivity return <div style={{ left: position.x }} />;

good.code: return <div style={{ left: store.position.x }} />; // Maintains reactivity

debugging-checklist.item: Check if reactive values are accessed inside tracking scopes
Verify store updates use proper setters (not direct mutation)
Look for console.log statements in hot code paths
Ensure event handlers don't break propagation unnecessarily
Check for multiple unmatched updates that should be batched
Verify TypeScript errors aren't preventing compilation
